claims.text: refund-requirements.md at stage-2: staff refund by hand on the admin page of the payment gateway, run by a separate provider; YC-9 asks that no order is refunded twice even when sending to the gateway is retried.
At stage-2 Order owns its status rules through the methods Cancel, Ship and MarkPaid, in DonHang.Domain (the team's own code).
stage-1 signed its own tokens and hashed passwords; stage-2 removed JwtTokenService and PasswordHasher (and AuthController, POST /api/v1/auth/login) and hands sign-in to Keycloak.
Keycloak runs as the keycloak service in docker-compose.yml at stage-2 (image quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7.4, command start-dev --import-realm).

MailKitEmailSender implements IEmailSender with MailKit; only this class knows MailKit. MailKit is a package run in the API's process, no extra service. Line 29: the lab's Mailpit speaks plain SMTP (the protocol for sending email).

The keycloak service pins its image (193), sets an admin password (199) and KC_HOSTNAME (202), imports the realm file (208) holding the donhang realm's roles, the DonHang.App client and users; lines 190-191: start-dev keeps data in the container.
Keycloak and MailKit are open source and charge no licence fee (MailKit: MIT License, 'free of charge'; Keycloak: described as open source on keycloak.org).

claims.text: A build-vs-buy decision chooses between building a capability in the team's code, buying a product or a service someone else runs, and adopting open source (code anyone may use and run with no licence fee) the team runs itself.

A common default: build the core domain, buy or adopt generic subdomains, unless no product fits or the team must control something no product offers; a supporting subdomain like the product list takes the same branch and is built simply.

Returning money is critical but does not set Đơn Hàng apart, and the gateway does it, so refunds are bought; the gateway moves the money, and what Đơn Hàng writes (placed by ADR 0003) is taking the request and passing it on.
claims.source_hint: Outline items 2, 5; refund-requirements.md YC-1..YC-6; management.l3.weighing-options-in-an-adr summary line 2

claims.text: Adopting a whole server like Keycloak brings far more work than adopting a library like MailKit: setting, checking on each upgrade and backing up the server and its data are the team's job; MailKit adds only its package version.
Building in-house is not cheaper merely because there is no licence fee: the team pays with its own time to write the code and keep it working.
Open source moves cost from an invoice to the team's work (install, configure, upgrade, back up); a pinned image tag changes only when the team changes it.
